OCA2 diagnosis is confirmed by compound heterozygous OCA2 variants. Nystagmus, photophobia, and strabismus are mentioned as general OCA features but not attributed to this specific patient, so they are borderline.

Several extracted 'HPO terms' (giant platelets, Döhle-like bodies, abnormal leukocyte mitochondria, increased leukocyte copper) are findings described in the text but are not standard/valid HPO phenotype terms; giant platelets could map to 'Increased mean platelet volume' but is questionably a standard term as written.

'Poor reactions' is a vague finding better captured as lethargy/drowsiness. Methionine elevation and proline elevation are lab findings from the second boy; methionine is only mildly borderline elevated. Neonatal death of both affected boys is salient and missed.

This is a veterinary (feline) case, but the described syndrome is acquired pseudohypoaldosteronism with hyperkalemic type IV RTA; all extracted terms are supported by the text (stranguria/pollakiuria/hematuria, azotemia, hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, acidosis, nephrolithiasis, lethargy, anorexia, dehydration).

Diagnosis of sitosterolemia is well supported by clinical, genetic (ABCG5), and biochemical findings. Stomatocytosis and giant platelets are not described in this truncated text, and peripheral neuropathy is not explicitly stated (sensory findings suggest but do not confirm it).

The text clearly establishes Brugada syndrome as the diagnosis, and all extracted HPO terms (syncope, type 1 Brugada ECG pattern, left anterior hemiblock, ventricular tachycardia/torsade de pointes, ventricular fibrillation, sudden cardiac death) are supported by the case description.

Triangular face and macrodontia are described as general KBG features in the intro but not documented in this specific patient; the patient's facial dysmorphisms were bushy eyebrows and micrognathia. Small head circumference (5th percentile) supports microcephaly.

Elevated CK-MB was measured but not a phenotype term per se; myoglobinuria is not supported (myohemoglobin was serum myoglobin, not urinary); 'intraventricular systolic block' is a malformed term (ECG showed intraventricular/heart block); DCM was discussed generally but the patient's echo showed dilation with systolic dysfunction rather than a confirmed DCM diagnosis. Salient features like renal failure, coagulation disorders, AV block, elevated LDH, and gallstones were missed.
